title: refactor(ci): simplify workflows, consolidate lint/test/release, bump actions & deps
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Our repo has accumulated a large number of GitHub Actions workflow files with overlapping responsibility (lint, test, release). This increases maintenance burden and causes duplicated configuration drift across services and SDKs. This PR consolidates lint/test/release workflows into a smaller set of well-documented, reusable workflows, bumps core Actions to latest stable versions, and removes deprecated matrix entries.

What this changes: consolidated workflows are implemented under .github/workflows/ with clear entry points for lint, unit-test, integration-test, and release. Shared steps and Docker cache logic are moved to scripts/ci/utils.sh and action-templates/. Node toolchains are standardized to Node 20 in build matrix for JS/TS SDKs and to the documented runner labels for native builds. Deprecated per-repo job matrices were removed and replaced with a canonical matrix generator (scripts/ci/matrix.sh).

Checklist: - [x] Consolidate workflow files (lint/test/release) - [x] Bump actions/setup-node and actions/cache to recommended versions - [x] Abstract shared steps to scripts/ci/utils.sh - [x] Run full CI across redwood, redwood-sdk-python and redwood-sdk-typescript - [x] Update README_CI.md with migration notes - [x] Rollback plan documented

Testing & validation: Ran CI across monorepo; locally validated lint and unit test jobs. Integration tests were run against a staging infra job and two intermittent e2e flakes were investigated (see review convo). The change does not modify runtime behavior or production deployment artifacts.

Migration notes: Repositories using custom workflow fragments should move to the new action-templates directory; small wrapper workflows are provided to preserve compatibility. See README_CI.md for step-by-step migration.

Related: Linear ENG-7812 (CI consolidation), ENG-7841 (actions version bump), Jira SUP-4128 (support spike; infra flakiness).
